memory_update.text: POWL should be tracked as a direct engineered electrical-equipment/switchgear candidate for the grid-hardening node, but later layers must separate utility/grid demand from oil, gas, petrochemical, LNG, and commercial/industrial backlog.

MYRG is a cleaner underfollowed contractor candidate than many diversified infrastructure firms because its T&D segment maps directly to utility transmission, distribution, substation, maintenance, and repair work.
PLPC is a niche small-cap component supplier worth retaining as a second-order line-hardware and network-maintenance hypothesis; verify energy-network revenue mix before upgrading.

Need a follow-up pass on public grid-monitoring, wildfire-risk software, inspection, relay/protection, and sensor companies; many search hits were private, so public-market mapping remains incomplete.

For this node, the likely chokepoints are not only transformers and headline OEMs; qualified electrical contractors, engineered switchgear/power-control systems, line hardware, field services, inspection, and monitoring may be equally important.
